page.layout: One column of text with a title block above it. Marginal notes in the left margin. Running head at top right. Catchword at bottom right.

head.i: Sanctorum Patrum disertissima testimonia, quibus docent, opera insignissima (qua sunt passiones Sanctorum) non esse omnino condigna vitâ æternâ.

main_text.head: SECT. III.
main_text.p: Disertissima ea esse diximus, quia non nisi de essentiali beatitudine loquuntur, & non tantùm Passionum, sed & Patientium di-gnitatem pensitant.

Primus erit {*}Cyprianus: NON SUNT CONDIGNÆ PASSIONES,&c. Cùm (nempe) beati erimus, dignatione Domini honorati. Sic ille. Ubi Dignatio Dei certissimè Patien-tium ipsorum dignitatem qualemcunque sub-indicat.In epist. ad Thebaritanos. 56.

Secundus, {d}Athanasius: Nec universo orbi renunciantes, dignum aliquid habita-culis possu-mus[?] compensare cœlestibus. Loquitur genera-liter de optimis omnibus operibus, & de quovis cœlesti habitaculo.In vitam S. Antonii, citante Bel-larmino,lib. 5.de Justif. cap. 14. § Huc eti-am.

Tertius, {e}Ambrosius: NON SUNT CON-DIGNÆ, &c. Pro Christo dicimur pati, cùm non illi, sed nobis proficiat, quod patimur: sed ille [Christus] quia quærit occasionem remune-randi nos, hoc præcipit. Ut profusus enim lar-gitor, causam quærit quomodo donet indigno aut verecundus. Denique, ut ipsa exitia tole-rari possint, ipse vires suggerit. Rursus idem {f}Ambrosius:In textum Apostoli.

page.notes: Running head: only ANTIDOTUM is printed as title; "Cap. 14." at top right is a chapter number and was left out. The reference mark before Ambrosius in the main text is a small bullet, read as "e" from the matching margin note. The mark "f" at the foot of the page has no matching note visible on this scan, so it may belong to a note on the facing or next page. Italic and underline in the Ambrosius quotation and "vires suggerit" are read from the scan and may not be exact. The word "possumus" is partly obscured and is marked [?].
